title: Grateful Dead Live at University of Virginia on 1982-09-14
lineage: 1st Set: Beyer M160 -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN2nd Set: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Audience recording captures a hot ’82 show with a smoking Space→Aiko jam and a killer China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers an energetic early‑80s performance that many fans cite as one of the era’s gems – the space into Aiko, the seamless China Cat → Rider segue, and Jerry’s “hot hot hot” guitar on High Time stand out.  The audience source is surprisingly clear despite the sweaty gym atmosphere, though a few moments sound a bit muffled or “bacon‑crackling”.  Overall the music outweighs any minor sonic quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews, most rating 5 stars and praising both performance and sound; only a handful of mixed comments. The show is consistently described as high‑energy with standout jams, while the audience recording is noted as good to excellent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear enough to hear details; ambient crowd noise and gym humidity present. Some reviewers note occasional mic crackle (“bacon” sound) but overall the tape is listenable and captures the room’s energy.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set tight and well‑played, leading into a long Space that blossoms into the iconic Aiko jam. Six songs precede drums, then another six after the space, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised – “sweet”, “hot hot hot” guitar and vocal passion on High Time and other jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted smoking his monitor at the end of Rider; several reviewers mention strong bass (“Phil bombs”) and that Phil is surprisingly clear in this SBD mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for his interplay with Jerry during the Space→Aiko jam, described as “cool” and “wonderful”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s playing singled out on the second set, especially during China Cat and its transition into Rider.
